tasks.q: What are the three parts of computational thinking?
tasks.fb: All three appear in this topic, and all three are examinable by name.

tasks.q: Which part of computational thinking is each activity?
items: Deciding a train timetable only needs times and stations
Ignoring the colour of a car in a traffic simulation
Splitting a game into scoring, drawing and input
Listing the smaller problems inside a big one
Writing the steps to find the largest number
Working out the order the checks must happen in
tasks.fb: Remove detail, break it up, work out the steps.

tasks.q: What does abstraction mean in computational thinking?
a: Removing detail that is not needed to solve the problem
tasks.fb: The detail is removed from the model, not from the code.

tasks.q: Why is what counts as 'unnecessary' not fixed?
a: It depends on the problem: a detail that matters in one model is noise in another
Because different people prefer different details
tasks.fb: Road surface matters to a road planner and not to a satnav.

tasks.q: Which details does a school register need? Select all that apply.
opts: Which form group they are in
correct: Which form group they are in
tasks.fb: Everything else is real, but irrelevant to taking a register.

tasks.q: Why is storing unnecessary data a problem?
a: It takes more space, slows the system and gives more to keep accurate and secure
It makes the screen look busy
It uses more electricity in the CPU
tasks.fb: There is a privacy cost too, from topic 1.6.

tasks.q: For a satnav, is each detail necessary or unnecessary?
items: The speed limit on a road
Whether a road is one way
How many trees line the road
The name of the road's builder
tasks.fb: Necessary means the route would change without it.

tasks.q: A flight simulator ignores the weight of the paint on the aircraft. Why is that acceptable?
a: It is far too small to change the behaviour being modelled
It would be illegal to include it
tasks.fb: Abstraction is about judging what makes a difference.

tasks.q: How is a subprogram an example of abstraction?
a: You use it by name without needing to know how it works inside
It runs faster than normal code
tasks.fb: The detail still exists; it is just hidden from whoever calls it.

tasks.q: Why do layers of abstraction matter in a large project?
a: Each person can work on their layer without understanding all the others
They remove the need for testing
tasks.fb: Nobody could hold an entire modern system in their head at once.

tasks.q: Which is the strongest exam answer about a library system?
a: It stores the title, author and whether a book is on loan, but not the paper weight, because that never affects lending
tasks.fb: Named details, plus the reason they are or aren't needed.

tasks.q: A question asks how abstraction has been used in an underground map. What earns the marks?
a: Naming what was removed, such as true distances and surface geography, and why that helps a passenger

tasks.q: For a cycle hire app, is each detail necessary or unnecessary?
items: How many bikes are free at each station
Whether a route has a cycle lane
The make of each bike's bell
The name of the street's architect
What colour the docking station is painted
Which shops are on the route
tasks.fb: Necessary means the app would behave differently without it.

info.title: Where the word comes from
info.text: To abstract something originally meant to draw it away. In computing you draw the important parts away from everything else.

info.title: The famous map
info.text: Harry Beck's 1933 underground diagram threw away real distances and geography, and became the model for transit maps worldwide.

info.title: Wrong but useful
info.text: The statistician George Box wrote that all models are wrong but some are useful, which is abstraction in five words.

info.title: Too much abstraction
info.text: Remove something that mattered and the model gives confident wrong answers, which is worse than no model at all.

info.title: Abstraction in hardware
info.text: You type a letter without knowing which transistors switched. Every layer below your program is hidden by abstraction.

info.title: Exam tip
info.text: Questions often show a picture and ask how abstraction was used. Name the details removed, not just the fact that some were.
